lessons.title: Flex Containers and Flex Items: display: flex, flex-direction and gap

objectives.cognitive: Explain what display: flex does to a box's children, and what flex-direction and gap control.
objectives.affective: Value a layout whose spacing is set in one place instead of on every item.
objectives.psychomotor: Turn Juan's skills list and project list into flex containers in CodeShare.

blocks.markdown: **How to use this module:** Work in order, Monday to Friday. Run every sample unchanged first, then do its small task. Answer each day's exit slip after its last step.

**Everything happens in CodeShare.** Open your class, then **Module**, this week and a step. **Work in code editor** loads the step's sample files into the editor tabs; **Run code** shows the step's run page in the page window and checks it, and its links open the project's other pages there. It works online and from the classroom laptop; no internet, installation, download or account is needed.

**Reading the outputs:** an output box shows the page text CodeShare checks for the step's run page: the Tab title, the Visible page text, then, on Steps 1, 3, 4, 5, 8 and 9, Media checks. Flexbox and media queries move boxes, so most steps this week leave the output exactly as it was; Step 4 and Step 8 are the two that change it, because they change whether an item is a box of its own. Spaces count.

**Where we start:** Juan's finished Week 8 site (three pages and styles.css) carries forward in your module project. Each step loads its run page and every file it needs; boxes show only new or changed lines.
**Week 9 starts here:** Juan's skills, project cards and form fields each carry their own margin, so changing the spacing means editing every rule.

display: flex on a box makes it a flex container, and every child becomes a flex item laid out in one direction. flex-direction: row puts the items across, column puts them one under the other, and gap sets the space between them in one place instead of a margin on each item. A flex item is a box of its own, so the output gives it its own line even when the page window shows the items side by side.

A jeepney bench: the passengers are the items and the bench is the container. The driver does not ask each passenger to leave a gap; the bench sets one spacing for everybody (gap), and the row either runs along the bench (row) or up the aisle (column).

an item that does not fit moves to the next line

blocks.markdown: **Media steps:** Steps 1, 3, 4, 5, 8 and 9 run index.html, with Juan's picture, sound, video and gallery pictures, files your teacher adds under Media files. Online, CodeShare checks them automatically; Run code waits on Loading media… until they are on this device. Offline, these six steps show Checked by your teacher for now, and your teacher presses Mark done. Steps 2, 6 and 7 run projects.html or contact.html and are checked automatically. Step 3's task reuses a picture Juan already has, so there is no new media file this week.

blocks.instruction: Juan's Week 8 site carries forward. Flexbox arranges the boxes inside one box. You write display: flex on the container, and its children become its flex items. flex-direction: column puts them one under the other, and gap: 0.5em leaves an even space between them, with no margin to count. Juan's skills list is the container; each skill is an item. Run index.html unchanged.

blocks.markdown: **Practice: does it change the output?** (a) display: flex on .skills; (b) gap: 2em instead of 0.5em; (c) flex-direction: row on .skills; (d) display: inline on .skills li. Answers: (a) no: a list item was already a box of its own; (b) no: spacing is not page text; (c) no: each item keeps its own line; (d) yes: the two skills run together on one line.

**Page checks and the width of the window:** a page check reads a computed value, so it must be a value that is the same at every width. That is why no step from Step 5 on checks flex-direction on the nav list or on the project cards: those are the two values a media query changes. The checks read display, flex-wrap, the list style and the counts instead, and you test the width yourself by making the browser window narrower.
Answer the Monday exit slip now.

lessons.title: Flexbox Instead of Float: The Gallery and the Nav Bar

objectives.cognitive: Compare float and flexbox for a row of boxes, and say why flex-wrap replaces clear.
objectives.affective: Appreciate a simpler way to do what used to need several rules.
objectives.psychomotor: Rebuild Juan's gallery and nav bar with flexbox and read what changed in the output.

blocks.markdown: **Today's starting point:** Juan's gallery still floats, which needs a margin on every figure and clear: both on every heading; his nav items are inline-block words.

A float pulls one box out of the normal flow: the boxes after it wrap around it, every figure needs its own margin, and a heading needs clear: both to get below the row. A flex container arranges its items without taking them out of the flow: flex-wrap: wrap moves an item that does not fit onto the next line, gap spaces them, and nothing below needs clear. float is ignored on a flex item.

Water poured around a stone in a stream takes the stone out of the flow and everything bends around it (float); chairs set out in rows for a programme leave the floor plan intact and simply start a new row when one fills up (flex-wrap).

rows: A box that does not fit
drops below and may leave a hole
`flex-wrap: wrap` starts a clean next line
nothing: the container keeps its place in the flow

blocks.instruction: Flexbox replaces float. In Week 7 each gallery figure floated left and needed its own margin, with clear: both on the headings. Now .gallery is the flex container: display: flex puts the figures side by side, gap: 12px spaces them, and flex-wrap: wrap moves a figure that does not fit to the next line. The figures keep their width and lose float and margin. Run index.html unchanged.

lessons.title: One Page, Two Widths: Media Queries

objectives.cognitive: Read a media query and say which rules apply at which widths, and why a query must not change the page text.
objectives.affective: Show concern for classmates whose only computer is a phone.
objectives.psychomotor: Add two media queries to Juan's stylesheet and test them by making the browser window narrower.

blocks.markdown: **Today's starting point:** Juan's layout is the same at every width: on a narrow screen the nav bar is cramped and the cards waste the space beside them.

@media (max-width: 900px) { ... } wraps rules in a condition: the browser uses them only while the page is 900 pixels wide or narrower, and re-reads the condition whenever the width changes. The width is the page's, not the screen's, so a narrower browser window turns a query on: the page window follows the browser window, and you cannot drag the page window itself. A query may change how boxes sit, never the words on the page: a step's expected output must be the same at every width.
A folding sari-sari store: open on a wide pavement it spreads its goods in a row; on a narrow one it stacks them. Same goods, same words on the price list, different arrangement.

rows: the page is 900px wide or narrower
the nav column and the row of project cards
not used: the rules outside the query already cover it
never: a length needs its unit, so the query is dropped
the page's width, not the screen's
a narrower browser window turns the query on
only how boxes sit, never the words
so a step's output is the same at every width

blocks.instruction: A media query gives a rule a condition. @media (max-width: 900px) { ... } means: use the rules inside only while the page is 900 pixels wide or narrower. Inside it, nav ul gets flex-direction: column, so on a narrow page the nav items stand one under the other and each one is easy to tap. Nothing outside the query changes. Run index.html unchanged.

lessons.title: When a Flex Container Disappears: Repairs, then Start Your Own

objectives.cognitive: Recognise a layout whose flex container was removed, and tell display: inline from a flex item.
objectives.affective: Show patience and care when three deleted lines change a whole layout.
objectives.psychomotor: Repair Juan's skills list, then begin the personal flexbox and media query.

blocks.markdown: **Today's starting point:** Three lines deleted from one rule can undo a whole layout, and the browser shows no error.

If display: flex is missing or misspelt, there is no flex container: gap does nothing, flex-direction does nothing, and the items fall back to their own display. display: inline on a list item makes it run together with the next one like words, which does change the page text. A media query with no units, @media (max-width: 900), is dropped whole.
A shelf with its brackets removed: nothing is missing from the books, but they are all in a heap.

blocks.instruction: Flexbox for a form. form becomes a flex container with flex-direction: column and gap: 0.75em, so every field is a flex item with the same space above and below it. The fields were already one under the other, but each carried its own paragraph margin; one gap now sets the spacing for all of them. Run contact.html unchanged.

rows.see: gap and flex-direction do nothing, and the items keep their old spacing.
rows.means: display: flex is missing or misspelt, so there is no flex container.
rows.fix: Write display: flex; on the container, not on the items.

rows.see: The list items run together on one line, in the page window and in the output.
rows.means: display: inline on the items, with no flex container above them.
rows.fix: Delete that rule and put display: flex back on the container.

rows.see: A whole media query does nothing at any width.
rows.means: A length has no unit: @media (max-width: 900) is dropped.

rows.see: The items are side by side when you wanted them stacked.
rows.means: flex-direction is row, which is what a flex container does by default.
rows.fix: Add flex-direction: column; to the container.

rows.see: An item that does not fit squeezes the others instead of moving down.
rows.means: flex-wrap is missing, so the row never breaks.
rows.fix: Add flex-wrap: wrap; to the container.

performanceTask.title: My Resume, Week 9: Flexbox and a Media Query
performanceTask.markdown:
Start Thursday; finish and present Friday. In CodeShare open Projects, then Personal performance-task project. Your Week 8 site carries forward: add this week's rules to your own styles.css.

Turn at least two boxes of your own site into flex containers: your skills list, your gallery, your nav bar or your form. On each one write display: flex, choose flex-direction, and set the spacing with gap instead of a margin on every item; add flex-wrap: wrap to any row that may run out of width. Then add at least one media query, @media (max-width: 900px), that makes your layout better on a narrow page: stack your nav items, or turn a column of cards into a wrapping row. Nothing inside the query may add, remove or re-letter a word: your output must be the same at every width. Your own project's page fills the page window, so whether your query is on depends on your browser window's width: make it narrower if the query is off, wider if it is already on. The page window follows the browser window and cannot be dragged on its own. Flexbox and media queries work the same online and offline; offline your gallery pictures still show only their alt text until you add them online.

Use only safe details: no home address, phone number, birth date, ID numbers or personal social-media accounts, and no other people in any picture. Run code until index.html runs with no error, then press Submit this version. Saving or running is not submitting.

Thursday: 0–60 min, repairs and the strip; 60–120 min, plan on paper, show the teacher, then start. Friday: 0–30 min, finish and run; 30–105 min, presentations; 105–120 min, strip and Submit this version.
checklist: Keep your Week 8 site: every page, the nav bar, the gallery, your states and decorations, and styles.css on every page.
At least two flex containers of your own, each with display: flex and a flex-direction you chose.
gap on every flex container, instead of a margin on each item.
flex-wrap: wrap on any row that could run out of width.
At least one media query, @media (max-width: 900px), that improves the narrow layout.
Nothing inside a media query adds, removes or re-letters a word: the output is the same at every width.
Nothing in url(); no address, phone, birth date, ID numbers, social media or other people in a picture.
Run code shows no error; resizing the browser window shows your query working; press Submit this version, then present.
